transcript.text: Our Dyson (one of the V ones, purple bits) keeps cutting out after about 5-10 seconds. Not every time - some days it does a whole room fine. It's maybe 5 years old. Already cleaned the filter and checked for blockages. Battery or something else?

It could be the battery, but because it sometimes runs fine, it might also be the vacuum protecting itself from restricted airflow. Please charge the vacuum fully (leave it on the charger for at least 3.5 hours until the light is steady), then run it on normal mode (not Boost/Max) on hard floors with no attachments. Does it now run for its usual time, or does it still cut out after a few seconds?

I haven't done that exact test yet, but it's usually fine straight off the charger and gets worse once the battery's partly used. On Max it nearly always stops within a few seconds. The battery isn't swollen or hot, if that matters. Is that enough to say whether it's the battery?

That pattern is very typical of a battery that has lost its capacity. When it’s fresh off the charger, the voltage looks okay, but as soon as you draw power (especially in Max mode), the internal resistance causes the voltage to drop below the safety threshold, triggering an immediate cut-out. Since you’ve already cleaned the filter and checked for blockages, and the machine is five years old, it’s probably the battery pack itself. Dyson batteries are user-replaceable on most V-series models (usually just a couple of screws). I’d recommend buying an official replacement or a high-quality third-party one from a reputable seller. Once you swap it out, the issue should be resolved.
